title: "Latent Variable Perspective"

**Study reference:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning*, §10.7. The examples, reasoning and notation explanations are written independently.

## Start from a problem

PCA can also be interpreted as a model in which low-dimensional hidden coordinates generate observed high-dimensional data. The probabilistic perspective makes noise and uncertainty explicit.

## Formulate the problem mathematically

$$
\boldsymbol z\sim\mathcal N(0,I),\quad\boldsymbol x=W\boldsymbol z+\boldsymbol\mu+\boldsymbol\varepsilon,\quad\boldsymbol\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I)
$$

This relation identifies the required structure. Interpret the symbols using the stated model rather than memorising the formula without its assumptions.

## Derive a worked result

Think of an order as having an unobserved 'size/complexity' factor z that affects both route distance and item count. The matrix W maps this factor into the two measured coordinates, while epsilon represents unexplained variation.

## Why the mathematics matters

This is a simplified probabilistic PCA-style generative model; its noise assumptions are stronger than classical deterministic PCA. A latent variable is a model construct, not automatically a discovered physical cause.

## Explain or calculate

What happens to the covariance of x when the isotropic noise variance sigma² increases?
